papers.title: Cycle Counting and Character Expectations Using Alternating Structures
papers.abstract: Recently, three related papers [arXiv:2412.13941, arXiv:2009.00897, arXiv:2409.03626] found a connection between two subjects: the w-cycle theorem, which is a theorem about counting appearances of cycles reading out a word w in certain graphs, and character expectations on word measures. The w-cycle theorem was proven independently by [arXiv:1410.2540] using stackings and by [arXiv:1410.2579] using bislim structures. In the current work, we generalize stackings and bislim structures to alternating stackings and alternating bislim structures. We show how this significantly strengthens the w-cycle theorem for words admitting such alternating structures, and as a result, also strengthens the recent results of [arXiv:2412.13941] and [arXiv:2409.03626]. We show that generic words admit alternating bislim structures, and therefore, the strengthened results hold for generic words. Using our new machinery, we address conjectures of Wilton, of Hanany--Puder and of Puder--Shomroni. We prove that all three conjectures hold for generic words, but we also find counterexamples for the first two.

papers.title: The mean orders of even and odd permutations
papers.abstract: We compare the sums of the orders of the even and odd permutations of a given degree. For all large degrees the odd permutations have the larger sum. The excess equals the sum of orders of the permutations of odd order up to a relative error decaying faster than any power of the degree. Following Goh and Schmutz, we determine the logarithm of this sum over the group order asymptotically, with an explicit constant. Hence the ratio of the sums of element orders of the symmetric and alternating groups tends to two from above. The proof rests on an exact identity for generating functions. It isolates cycles of length a large prime times a small factor. Inclusion and exclusion over small odd primes enlarges this family. Each Euler factor is bounded by its maximum modulus. All constants are certified in ball arithmetic. Exact values up to degree 150 suggest that the odd permutations have the larger sum from degree four on.

papers.title: Compactness-like properties in Alexandroff paratopological groups
papers.abstract: We study compactness-like and covering properties in non-compact Alexandroff paratopological groups. Several properties are characterized in terms of the order structure associated with the Alexandroff topology and the number of connected components. We establish equivalences among $2$-pseudocompactness, countable $o$-compactness, Baire, and an intersection property for increasing chains. We also obtain a common characterization of $\sigma$-local compactness, $\sigma$-compactness, the Lindel\"of property, and left $\omega$-precompactness in terms of the existence of a countable cofinal subset. Moreover, we characterize pseudocompactness, $H$-compactness, star-compactness, the countable chain condition, and the weakly Lindel\"of property by means of the number of connected components. Finally, we determine further implications among the properties considered and provide examples and counterexamples.

papers.title: Codimension two complements in hyperbolic products
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-volume locally symmetric manifold modeled on $\H^m \times \H^n$, and let $S$ be a compact, totally geodesic, codimension two submanifold of $M$ modeled on $\H^{m-1} \times \H^{n-1}$. In this paper, we initiate the study of manifolds of the form $N = M \setminus S$. In the case where $M$ is a product and $S$ is connected, we prove that such $N$ admit complete, finite-volume, $A$-regular metrics with non-positive sectional curvature. We also deduce some topological properties of $N$, and algebraic properties of $\pi_1(N)$. In the case where $M$ is irreducible, we show that $N$ admits {\it almost non-positive curvature}. Similar results hold for manifolds $X_d$, which are $d$-fold branched covers of $M$ ramified over $S$. Along the way, we show that there are infinitely many commensurability classes of such pairs $(M,S)$, and develop general curvature formulas for doubly warped product metrics, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Explicit Bases for the Second Integral Homology of Cactus Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the second integral homology $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$ of cactus groups $J_n$. We first use Hopf's formula and Pontryagin products to obtain a smaller generating set of $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$. We then construct a detecting homomorphism to prove that these generators are linearly independent and hence form an explicit basis.

papers.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.

papers.title: Local Statistics of Random Permutations from Free Products
papers.abstract: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be uniformly random permutations of orders $2$ and $3$, respectively, in $S_{N}$, and consider, say, the permutation $\alpha\beta\alpha\beta^{-1}$. How many fixed points does this random permutation have on average? The current paper studies questions of this kind and relates them to surprising topological and algebraic invariants of elements in free products of groups. Formally, let $\Gamma=G_{1}*\ldots*G_{k}$ be a free product of groups where each of $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ is either finite, finitely generated free, or an orientable hyperbolic surface group. For a fixed element $\gamma\in\Gamma$, a $\gamma$-random permutation in the symmetric group $S_{N}$ is the image of $\gamma$ through a uniformly random homomorphism $\Gamma\to S_{N}$. In this paper we study local statistics of $\gamma$-random permutations and their asymptotics as $N$ grows. We first consider $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$, the expected number of fixed points in a $\gamma$-random permutation in $S_{N}$. We show that unless $\gamma$ has finite order, the limit of $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ as $N\to\infty$ is an integer, and is equal to the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ such that $H\cong\mathbb{Z}$ or $H\cong C_{2}*C_{2}$. Equivalently, this is the number of subgroups $H\le\Gamma$ containing $\gamma$ and having (rational) Euler characteristic zero. We also prove there is an asymptotic expansion for $\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{fix}_{\gamma}\left(N\right)\right]$ and determine the limit distribution of the number of fixed points as $N\to\infty$. These results are then generalized to all statistics of cycles of fixed lengths.

papers.title: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $\phi$ and $\psi$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\psi$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^\phi$ and $G_x^\psi$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $\phi$ and $\psi$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $\phi$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^\phi$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.

papers.title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\in\gamma_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for a word with six syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.

papers.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leq\Gamma_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.

papers.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.

papers.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/\Gamma$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $\Gamma$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to M\"obius conjugacy. The proof uses trace rigidity, dihedral surgery, half-turn symmetries, and an index-two cover.

papers.title: Profinite groups with coprime automorphisms whose orbits generate nilpotent subgroups
papers.abstract: Suppose that a profinite group $G$ admits a finite group of coprime automorphisms $A$ such that for any $\varphi\in A$ every subgroup $\langle x^{\langle\varphi\rangle}\rangle$ generated by the $\langle\varphi\rangle$-orbit of an element $x\in G$ is nilpotent. It is proved that $[G,A]$ is pronilpotent, and if $A$ is soluble and the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(A)$ is locally nilpotent, then $G$ is locally nilpotent.

papers.title: Random homomorphisms from affine to spherical reflection groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to understand the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)$ of homomorphisms from an affine reflection group $\widetilde{W}$ to its associated spherical reflection group $W$. We do this in three ways: numerically, by deriving an explicit formula for $|\mathrm{Hom}(\widetilde{W},W)|$; probabilistically, by exploring the question what does a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}\to W$ look like?; and algebraically, by explicitly writing down all possible homomorphisms on the standard generators. For example, we show that as $n\to\infty$ the probability that a random homomorphism $\widetilde{W}_n\to W_n$ is surjective tends to $\frac{3}{4}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n}$ or $D_n$, to $\frac{9}{16}$ if $W_n$ is of type $C_{2n+1}$, and to $1$ if $W_n$ is of type $A_n.$

papers.title: Blocks with one simple module and solvable groups
papers.abstract: Let $b$ be a block of a finite group with one isomorphism class of simple modules in characteristic $p$. We construct, over a sufficiently large complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero, a Morita equivalence between $b$ and a block of a finite solvable group. The proof uses equivariant Morita bimodules for the quasisimple blocks that occur in the component reduction. We also prove that a block over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ is nilpotent whenever it is Morita equivalent to the group algebra of a finite $p$-group. For the latter result, we establish a criterion for twisted group algebras using derivations of the basic algebra and group transfer.

papers.title: On a question of A.N. Skiba concerning the modularity of the lattice of $\sigma$-permutable subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $\sigma=\{\sigma_i\mid i\in I\}$ be some partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. A subgroup $A$ of $G$ is said to be $\sigma$-permutable in $G$ if $G$ has a Hall $\sigma_i$-subgroup for every $i\in I$ and $A$ permutes with every Hall $\sigma_i$-subgroup of $G$ for all $i\in I$. We describe the finite groups $G$ for which the lattice $\Lper(G)$ of all $\sigma$-permutable subgroups of $G$ is modular. This answers the first part of a question of A.N. Skiba. We also prove that if every Hall $\sigma_i$-subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent, then $\Lper(G)$ is modular if and only if every two members of $\Lper(G)$ are permutable.

papers.title: Berkovich's conjecture on noninner automorphisms of order $p$
papers.abstract: We prove a long-standing conjecture of Berkovich (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 4.13): every finite nonabelian $p$-group $P$ has a noninner automorphism of order $p$. If $p$ is odd, the automorphism $\alpha$ can be chosen with $[P,\alpha,\alpha]=1$. More precisely, given a maximal normal elementary abelian subgroup $E$ of $P$, we can choose $\alpha$ to fix both $F$ and $P/F$ pointwise, where $F$ is either $E$ or a hyperplane of $E$ normal in $P$. If $p=2$, the automorphism can be chosen with $[P,\alpha,\alpha,\alpha]=1$, and with $[P,\alpha,\alpha]=1$ when $Z(P)$ is noncyclic. The dihedral group of order eight shows that the hypothesis on $Z(P)$ cannot be omitted.

papers.title: On simultaneous left- and right-homometric sets on the positive affine line group
papers.abstract: On a non-abelian group $G$, the homometry problem comes in two flavors, depending on whether differences are computed on the left or on the right. A natural question is to determine whether simultaneously left- and right-homometric subsets of $G$ exist. This question has been answered positively in the case of dihedral groups by Genuys and Popoff. We here prove that no such subsets exist on the positive affine line group, if we impose that the subgroups generated by their left- and right-differences be non-abelian.

papers.title: Products of supersoluble groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=AB$ be a finite group, where $A$ and $B$ are supersoluble. We prove that every nonabelian composition factor of $G$ is isomorphic to $\PSL_2(p)$ for some prime $p\ge5$ and that the nonsoluble length of $G$ is at most one.

papers.title: Blocks of profinite group algebras and the extended Brauer correspondence
papers.abstract: We describe the centre of the completed group algebra of a profinite group and prove a generalisation of Brauer's Extended First Main Theorem to profinite groups.

papers.title: Form of Words in Free Products with scl 1/12
papers.abstract: Let $G = *_\lambda G_\lambda$ be a free product of groups and let $g\in G$ be any element not conjugate into any free factor and not conjugate to its inverse. Then $\mathrm{scl}(g) \ge \frac{1}{12}$ and $\mathrm{scl}(g) = \frac{1}{12}$ if and only if $g$ is a product of an element of order $2$ and an element of order $3$. In particular, this classifies all elements in $G = \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$ with $\mathrm{scl}_G(g) = \frac{1}{12}$.

papers.title: Every Finite Incline Is Finitely Based
papers.abstract: We prove that every incline of finite additive height generates a Cross variety. In particular, every finite incline is finitely based. Moreover, we obtain a uniform bound on the number of variables needed to axiomatize subvarieties of decreasing Catalan semiring varieties, and give an effective construction of finite equational bases.

papers.title: Groups with dual classes of subgroups
papers.abstract: We completely characterize insoluble groups whose subgroups are pronormal or pronormalize every subgroup. We also completely describe $p$-groups with this property, and prove many structural results in the soluble case (for example, such groups are always of length at most $3$ and have Sylow towers).

papers.title: Asymptotic insolubility of alternating groups
papers.abstract: Let $a,b\in\mathrm{Aut}(A_n)$ with $a\neq 1$, and let $s$ be chosen uniformly in $A_n$. We show that the probability that $\langle a, bs\rangle$ is insoluble tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$, uniformly in $a$ and $b$. More precisely, this probability is at least $1-O(n^{-1/24})$. The proof combines a bound in terms of the support of $a$ with estimates on permutations lying in transitive subgroups of the symmetric group.

papers.title: Finite simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes
papers.abstract: A theorem by Guralnick classifying finite simple groups with subgroups of prime power index implies that $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ is the unique finite non-abelian simple group whose maximal subgroups all have prime power index. Motivated by this result and appealing to Li and Li's classification of primitive permutation groups of degree $p^a q^b$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, we classify all finite non-abelian simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes, proving that they are precisely $A_5$, $A_6$, $A_7$, $A_8$, ${\rm PSL}(2,7)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,8)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,11)$, ${\rm PSp}(4,3)$, ${\rm PSU}(3,3)$, and ${\rm PSU}(3,4)$.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity and zero divisors in random graphical groups
papers.abstract: We give a criterion for hyperbolicity of random groups presented by labelled graphs. On $n$ vertices, we prescribe the proportions of the possible sets of outgoing labels. For each generator, we choose a uniform matching between its occurrences and those of its inverse, independently across generators. We condition the graph to have girth at least $\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$ for sufficiently small $c>0$, and take the labels of closed paths as relators. The distribution of outgoing labels determines a matrix of turn weights. Suppose that each letter occurs as often as its inverse and with positive frequency, every vertex has degree at least three, and the entrywise square of the turn matrix has spectral radius less than one. We prove that, with probability tending to one as $n$ grows, the resulting group is torsion-free and non-elementary hyperbolic and admits a finite two-dimensional classifying space. On the same event, every path from a prescribed root to a different vertex has nontrivial label in the group. The proof uses the spectral radius bound to control repeated path labels in diagrams and a local-to-global argument to obtain a linear isoperimetric inequality. Applied to OpenAI's characteristic-two zero-divisor construction, the criterion recovers the hyperbolicity result of Mghirbi and Douglas.

papers.title: Strong Banach property $(T)$ for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$
papers.abstract: Strong Banach property $(T)$ has been established for higher-rank algebraic groups over non-Archimedean local fields with respect to Banach spaces of nontrivial type. However, in the real setting, existing results have required additional geometric hypotheses on the Banach spaces, leaving the corresponding question open even for $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$. We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb R)$ has strong Banach property $(T)$ with respect to every class of complex Banach spaces of uniformly nontrivial Rademacher type.

papers.title: A hyperbolic 7-manifold that fibers over the circle
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit orientable finite-volume hyperbolic $7$-manifold $M$ that fibers over the circle. The manifold is tessellated by $256$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic polytope $P^7$ and has $252$ cusps. The fiber is the interior of a compact aspherical $6$-manifold whose boundary consists of $256$ five-dimensional tori. The fibration comes from a Bestvina-Brady Morse function on the Davis complex. Bestvina-Brady theory shows that the kernel of the associated character is finitely presented. A perturbation argument over the integral Novikov ring shows that the infinite cyclic cover is finitely dominated. Farrell's fibering theorem, together with the vanishing of the Whitehead group, then gives the fibration.

papers.title: Leavitt path algebras, growth series, Thompson groups
papers.abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Mart\'in Barquero, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.

papers.title: An example of a non-commutative division ring with abelian maximal subgroups
papers.abstract: We construct a cyclic division algebra $D$ of degree $6$ with center $F$ algebraic over $\Q$. The multiplicative group $K^\times$ of a maximal subfield $K$ is maximal in $D^\times$, disproving Conjecture~C of Akbari, Ebrahimian, Momenaee Kermani, and Salehi Golsefidy. The field norm $N_{K/F}$ maps $K^\times$ onto $F^\times$, and its kernel is maximal in the reduced norm-one group $D^{(1)}$. The quotient $D^{(1)}/Z(D^{(1)})$ is nonabelian simple, with the image of $\ker N_{K/F}$ as an abelian maximal subgroup. The proof uses matrix factorizations over local fields, a convolution theorem of Breuillard and Glazer, and Moret--Bailly's theorem on points over extensions with prescribed splitting.
